_schema: Ben's review queue. Canonical store; NEEDS_REVIEW.md is the readable mirror. Entry fields: id, title, raised (ISO date), kind, status, source, what, why_it_matters, options (array, only where there is a genuine fork), recommendation, files, resolution (null until Ben answers).
_note: Companion to backlog.json and review.json, NOT a replacement for either.
PURPOSE: things awaiting BEN'S JUDGEMENT. Three kinds live here:
- 'question'        â€” an open call nobody has made yet, usually surfaced by
doing adjacent work. Not blocking, or it would be a
backlog item with blocked_on set.
- 'decision-taken'  â€” a call made ON BEN'S BEHALF so work could continue.
Recorded here so it can be OVERTURNED rather than
quietly becoming precedent. This is the important half:
an unrecorded delegated decision is indistinguishable
from a decision Ben made.
- 'observation'     â€” something noticed in passing that is too small or too
cross-cutting to file, but which a human should see.
- 'novel-work'      â€” raised by a SESSION about its own task (Ben, 2026-08-20):
the work in hand feels NOVEL â€” no owning authority doc, no
saved role or established pattern fits, or it quietly grows
the project's scope. Raise it AT THE MOMENT the feeling
arises, then continue (or pause, if scope growth is large).
Gives Ben a drift detector: novelty should be chosen, not
accreted.
HOW IT DIFFERS FROM review.json: review.json is a BLOCKER list â€” items blocked
on a visual artifact only Ben can produce (a mockup, an annotated screenshot).
Work there cannot proceed at all. Entries here are not blocking; they are
questions and reversible calls. If an entry turns out to need a mockup, move it
to review.json and leave a resolution here pointing at it.
HOW IT DIFFERS FROM backlog.json: an entry here is not work. If Ben's answer
creates work, file a backlog item and resolve the entry with that item's id.
LIFECYCLE (revised 2026-08-14, Ben's ruling): this file is TRANSIENT â€” a live
queue of open calls, not a permanent audit trail. Append entries as they arise
and set status to 'resolved' with a resolution once answered, exactly as before.
But do NOT let resolved entries accumulate: prune them promptly rather than
holding them for posterity. The reasoning is not lost â€” it lands in code
comments, an authority doc, or a backlog item's design field at the moment the
work happens, and THAT is the durable record. Ben's own framing: 'the docs
should preserve changes made, and the review queue should only be for things
of that level of importance' â€” i.e. open and unresolved, not a history of
everything ever decided. A large housekeeping sweep this date closed 231
entries down to 2 genuinely open ones on this basis.

ARCHIVAL (2026-08-23): 'prune' now means MOVE, not delete. Run node tools/session/archive_reviews.js to move every resolved entry, verbatim, into docs/development/archive/needs-review-<quarter>.json, then re-render the mirror. The hot file holds open entries only.
SEEDED 2026-08-01 at Ben's request, populated from that session.

PURGE 2026-08-23: 240 open entries -> 18. Every entry referring only to backlog ids <= BL-568 (retired by the same-day backlog purge) was retired; 16 more were answered by reading the current docs and tree. All 223 are frozen verbatim in archive/needs-review-purged-2026-08-23.json, each with a resolution saying why. The survivors are asked as a form: tools/session/register/review_queue.js, built by register/build.js, published at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/53fb4e56-2eae-439e-bcb7-121fa49bd340 . NR-576 records the calls taken in the sweep.

DRAINED 2026-09-01 on Ben's instruction, from 117 open to 0. The queue had become a shadow backlog: most entries named WORK rather than a judgement, so ten backlog items (BL-713..BL-722) were minted to carry it and every entry was closed with a resolution saying where it went. THE RULE THAT KEEPS IT DRAINED, and it is now in CLAUDE.md Rule 0c: a call only Ben can make belongs here; work belongs in backlog.json; a fact worth remembering belongs in the comment or doc next to the code.

items.title: CALLS LEFT BY WAVE A: seven readings on merged work that only Ben can judge
items.source: Backlog wave A close-out. Ben stopped the backlog at wave A ("reinvent anything important later"), so these are recorded as calls rather than filed as work.
items.what:
1. COASTAL GROUND IS CHEAPER TO TAKE (BL-1022, your NR-828 ruling said a yes comes to you). Deaths per region taken over 16 seeds: inland 3,084, coastal 2,613 (about 15% cheaper, in 12 of 16 seeds), apparently from smaller coastal garrisons rather than the sea-legs ration; the cheapest route is the held-shore forage crossing (2,028). Is that the inversion you rejected?
2. TRADE RE-BASE HALF-HOLDS (BL-1021). Trade now helps a realm pay its armies but not its campaigns; and with only three trade classes a region earns at most 80 a year, so income grows with regions held, not with kinds of ground reached -- which was the reason for the re-base. The reach floor and the cross-border reading were chosen, not ruled.
3. SOLVENCY NO LONGER GATES THE SEAT (BL-1020). 74 of 84 shortlisted seats have a negative trailing net. The live click was never run.
4. THREE HARNESS ROWS WENT HONESTLY RED ON THE 12-TICK SETTLE (BL-1008): spawn_solvency R4 (no rival fields a standing force within 12 ticks -- read longer, reword as "can afford to hire", or stay red); acquisition_viability R1 (judges one quarter); and material_floor's "dead" definition (zero output across the whole settle).
5. SMALL GRUDGES NOW FADE LINEARLY (BL-842), faster than the design's 230-year half-life and faster on finer steps. Keeping the exact rate needs a stored remainder, which brings back stationary rounds.
6. THE CULTURE FOLD (BL-1017): a culture whose only ground is a future founding is not folded; kinship walks the living tree rather than coined_from. Neither moves any shipped world today.
7. DECISIONS TAKEN ON YOUR BEHALF: the far-trade reading's defaults (epoch 1960, first year of play, nearest by dispatcher pricing, cargo counted first) and the Digitisation readings' interpretations -- which generate at epoch 0 and so read "advanced chains" as zero by construction.

UPDATE 2026-09-17 (item 7): answered by BL-1029 (Digitisation readings at 1960). digitisation_sim_harness --through 1960 reads the shipped world continued to 1960 beside a fingerprint-checked 1660 control; "advanced chains" stays a STRUCTURAL ZERO there too, because the recipe band follows epoch_year, and now prints as one. The far-trade reading (haulage_measure) still runs epoch_year 1960, the superseded arc; it moves with the epoch flip. Items 1-6 unchanged.

UPDATE 2026-09-17 (item 3): the "74 of 84 shortlisted seats negative" figure came from player_seed_sweep before it reached app parity (BL-1030). On the app's world, over the 16 library seeds: 109 of 170 specialists shortlisted, 81 of the 109 (74.3%) with negative trailing net, every shortlisted seat with a processor, and a different corporation seated on every seed. The call stands; its number moved.
items.why_it_matters: Each sits on code now on main and re-blessed. None blocks anything, because the backlog is empty; they are the questions to settle before any of that work is picked up again.
items.recommendation: Take 1 and 2 whenever Exploration or the Era -1 economy is next touched; 3 before the seat canvas is designed (it sits beside NR-885); 4-7 can wait for the harness or item that next reads them.

items.title: CALL: a charter budget cannot raise a body's firm count above Pass 6's breadth cap — which ruling gives way?
items.source: BL-1032 (charter budget seam), its lane's novelty flag and cold review, on seed 0 with a synthetic budget (test input only).
items.what:
TWO RULINGS MEET. CORPORATION_GENERATION.md Pass 6 (Ben, 2026-09-06): density IS the per-resource firm cap — a body holds at most 8 firms per demanded good, so the count is exactly specialists + 8 x goods with demand. DIGITISATION.md § 1 (Ben, 2026-09-15/17): on a Digitisation world the budget decides how many firms stand where, and breadth only decides which goods.
WHAT THE SEAM SHOWS. The budget path keeps Pass 6's gap selection and its cap, so the cap still binds. Seed 0: the legacy landscape lays 81 background firms. A synthetic budget at 1x (87 points) charters 2 specialists and 79 firms and spends everything; at 4x (348 points) it charters 11 specialists and 81 firms and leaves 219 points unspent as no_gap across 204 centres. So a richer world moves firms toward its cities and adds specialists, but cannot make a body denser than breadth x 8.
OPTIONS. (a) Keep the cap: capital beyond breadth x 8 stays unspent, and density follows cities only in where firms stand, not how many there are. (b) Lift the per-resource cap on a budget world only: capital decides the count, bounded by the 200-per-body anti-runaway and by what each market can absorb. (c) Scale the cap with the body's charter capital. (b) and (c) amend the 2026-09-06 ruling for Digitisation worlds, and raise the live tick cost BL-1033 measures.

READINGS TAKEN ON YOUR BEHALF in the seam (reversible, none moves today's world): rung 2 of a charter's anchor is its centre's own region, not BL-283's home-plus-three; a specialist that finds no ground in either window is not chartered and its price is counted unspent (no asset-light specialist); a firm that fails to place ends that centre's firm spend; only a firm's anchor is held to the window — its other holdings walk outward as Pass 3 lays them, now reported by distance; the synthetic test budget weighs centres by a seeded 1/rank law so that a 1x budget can afford any specialist at all (population is never read).

UPDATE 2026-09-17 (Ben, elicitation): measure first. BL-1033 runs the per-resource cap kept and lifted side by side on budget worlds; the call is ruled on its tick cost and unspent points. The entry stays open until then.
items.why_it_matters: BL-1033 (charter budget cost) measures tick cost at 1x/2x/4x. Under (a) the 4x world is barely denser than 1x and the cost reading understates what Beat 1 could ask for; under (b) or (c) the measurement must lift the cap to mean anything. Better ruled before BL-1033 runs.
options: (a) keep the per-resource cap on budget worlds; capital beyond it stays unspent
(b) lift the per-resource cap on budget worlds; the 200-per-body cap and market absorption bound density
(c) scale the cap with the body's charter capital
items.recommendation: Measure (a) and (b) side by side in BL-1033 before ruling: the cost sweep already runs the province cap on and off, and the per-resource cap is the same kind of switch. Rule after reading tick cost and unspent points at 4x under both.
